```json
  "fix": "Use a safe signature `def add_job(job, queue=None):` and initialize inside the body with `if queue is None: queue = []` (or `queue = queue or []`), so each call gets a fresh list instead of the shared mutable default."

```

The bug: Python evaluates default arguments **once**, at `def` time — not per call. Since a list is mutable, all calls sharing the default mutate the same object.

The fix: the standard `None` sentinel pattern — default to `None`, then create a fresh list inside the function body.

## Step 1 — Define and Resolve the Workspace Boundary

```powershell
$workspace = Resolve-Path -LiteralPath 'C:\Work\MyProject' -ErrorAction Stop
$workspacePath = $workspace.Path.TrimEnd('\')
```

Resolve the workspace root first and fail immediately if it does not exist. Trimming the trailing backslash ensures consistent prefix comparisons later. Everything downstream is gated on this anchor.

## Step 2 — Resolve and Validate the Source Path

```powershell
$source = Resolve-Path -LiteralPath 'C:\Work\MyProject\old\reports' -ErrorAction Stop
$sourcePath = $source.Path.TrimEnd('\')

if (-not $sourcePath.StartsWith($workspacePath + '\', [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {
    throw "Source escapes workspace: $sourcePath"
}
if ($sourcePath -eq $workspacePath) {
    throw "Source must not be the workspace root itself"
}
```

`Resolve-Path` confirms the source exists and normalizes it to an absolute path. The ordinal, case-insensitive prefix check guarantees the source is strictly inside the workspace — never the root, never a sibling, never a path that escaped via symlinks or `..` segments (which `Resolve-Path` collapses). Fail closed: any violation aborts before any filesystem mutation.

## Step 3 — Resolve and Validate the Destination Parent

```powershell
$destParent = Resolve-Path -LiteralPath 'C:\Work\MyProject\archive' -ErrorAction Stop
$destParentPath = $destParent.Path.TrimEnd('\')

if (-not $destParentPath.StartsWith($workspacePath + '\', [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {
    throw "Destination escapes workspace: $destParentPath"
}
if ($destParentPath -eq $workspacePath) {
    if ($destParentPath -eq $sourcePath) {
        throw "Destination parent equals source"
    }
}
```

The destination parent must already exist and must also resolve strictly inside the workspace. This is the second fail-closed gate: if the parent directory is missing or resolves outside the boundary, the plan aborts rather than creating directories or moving data to an unintended location.

## Step 4 — Compute the Destination and Check for Collisions

```powerspace
$destName = Split-Path -Path $sourcePath -Leaf
$destPath = Join-Path -Path $destParentPath -ChildPath $destName

if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $destPath) {
    throw "Destination already exists: $destPath"
}
```

Derive the destination from the validated parent plus the source's leaf name, so the directory keeps its name. `Test-Path` with `-LiteralPath` refuses to overwrite anything — if the target exists, abort. This preserves unrelated files at the destination: nothing is merged, overwritten, or clobbered.

## Step 5 — Execute the Move with Literal Paths

```powershell
Move-Item -LiteralPath $sourcePath -Destination $destPath -ErrorAction Stop
```

Perform the single mutation only after all four validation gates pass. `-LiteralPath` ensures wildcard characters in directory names (`[`, `]`, `*`, `?`) are treated as literal characters, not patterns — so a directory named `data[old]` moves correctly instead of failing or matching unintended targets. `-ErrorAction Stop` makes any mid-move failure throw, and because `Move-Item` on a directory within the same volume is a metadata rename, the operation is atomic on NTFS: either the whole tree moves or nothing does.
